en: Saṃyutta Nikāya 37.1 (SN 37.1, PTS SN iv 238) 1. First Subsection on Repetition: Discourse on Women “Bhikkhus, women possess five qualities that lead to their being reborn in hell. What five? Here, bhikkhus, a woman is unattractive, she is of low birth, she is poor, she speaks harshly, and she is unfaithful. These are the five qualities that lead to a woman’s being reborn in hell. Bhikkhus, women possess five other qualities that lead to their being reborn in heaven. What five? Here, bhikkhus, a woman is beautiful, she is of noble birth, she is wealthy, she speaks kindly, and she is faithful. These are the five qualities that lead to a woman’s being reborn in heaven.”
“Bhikkhus, possessing five qualities, a woman is entirely displeasing to a man.
What are the five?
She is not beautiful; she does not possess wealth; she is not virtuous; she is lazy; and she does not bear children.”
“Monks, a woman endowed with these five qualities is entirely unappealing to a man.
Monks, a woman endowed with five qualities is entirely appealing to a man.
With which five?
“Monks, when a woman possesses these five factors, she is entirely pleasing to a man: she is beautiful, she is wealthy, she is virtuous, she is skillful and diligent, and she has offspring.
Monks, a woman endowed with these five factors is entirely pleasing to a man. Thus was the first [discourse].

Saṁyutta Nikāya 37.2 (SN 37.2, PTS SN iv 238) 1. First Subsection on Repetition: The Discourse on the Man “Bhikkhus, there are these three kinds of persons found existing in the world. What three? The person who is like a stone, the person who is like a water jar, and the person who is like a lotus. “And how, bhikkhus, is a person like a stone? Here, bhikkhus, when a man has gone to the monastery, he sits down on a seat made ready and engages in worldly talk. When the Dhamma is being taught by the Tathāgata—deep, profound, transcendent, dealing with the Void—he does not listen to it or lend an ear or apply his whole mind to understand it; and he finds no pleasure in hearing that Dhamma. Just as a stone of great size, thrown into a pool of water, sinks to the bottom without soaking through, so too, when a man has gone to the monastery... he finds no pleasure in hearing that Dhamma. This is called a person who is like a stone. “And how, bhikkhus, is a person like a water jar? Here, bhikkhus, when a man has gone to the monastery, he sits down on a seat made ready and engages in worldly talk. When the Dhamma is being taught by the Tathāgata—deep, profound, transcendent, dealing with the Void—he listens to it and lends an ear, but he does not apply his whole mind to understand it, and he finds no pleasure in hearing that Dhamma. Just as a water jar, when thrown into a pool of water, floats on the surface without soaking through, so too, when a man has gone to the monastery... he finds no pleasure in hearing that Dhamma. This is called a person who is like a water jar. “And how, bhikkhus, is a person like a lotus? Here, bhikkhus, when a man has gone to the monastery, he sits down on a seat made ready and engages in worldly talk. When the Dhamma is being taught by the Tathāgata—deep, profound, transcendent, dealing with the Void—he listens to it, lends an ear, and applies his whole mind to understand it, and he finds pleasure in hearing that Dhamma. Just as a blue, red, or white lotus, though born in the water and grown in the water, rises up above the water and stands unsoiled by the water, so too, when a man has gone to the monastery... he finds pleasure in hearing that Dhamma. This is called a person who is like a lotus. “These, bhikkhus, are the three kinds of persons found existing in the world.”
“Bhikkhus, a man endowed with five qualities is entirely unappealing to women.
With which five?
He is not handsome; he is not wealthy; he is not virtuous; he is lazy; and he does not obtain offspring.”
“Monks, a man endowed with these five qualities is exclusively displeasing to women.
Monks, a man endowed with five qualities is exclusively pleasing to women.
With which five?”
“He is handsome, he is wealthy, he is virtuous, he is skillful and diligent, and he gains offspring—
with these five factors, monks, a man is entirely pleasing to women. This is the second [sutta].

Saṃyutta Nikāya 37.3 (SN 37.3, PTS SN iv 239) 1. First Subsection on the Summary The Discourse on Individual Suffering "Bhikkhus, there are these five aggregates subject to clinging that are the individual suffering of a woman. What five? Whatever form [a woman] possesses, whether past, future, or present, internal or external, gross or subtle, inferior or superior, far or near—this is the first aggregate subject to clinging that is the individual suffering of a woman. Whatever feeling... whatever perception... whatever formations... whatever consciousness she possesses, whether past, future, or present, internal or external, gross or subtle, inferior or superior, far or near—this is the fifth aggregate subject to clinging that is the individual suffering of a woman. These, bhikkhus, are the five aggregates subject to clinging that are the individual suffering of a woman."
“Monks, there are these five unique sufferings of women that women experience, apart from men.
What are the five?
Here, monks, a woman, while still young, goes to her husband’s family; she is separated from her kinsfolk.”
This, monks, is the first unique suffering of women that women experience, apart from men.
Furthermore, monks, women undergo their period.
This, monks, is the second unique suffering of women that women experience, apart from men.
Furthermore, monks, a woman becomes pregnant.
This, monks, is the third unique suffering of women that women experience, apart from men.
Furthermore, monks, a woman gives birth.
This, monks, is the fourth distinct suffering of women that women experience, apart from men.
Furthermore, monks, women enter into service for men.
This, monks, is the fifth distinct suffering of women that women experience, apart from men.
“Monks, these are the five unique sufferings of women that women experience, apart from men.
This was the third [discourse]. *Saṃyutta Nikāya* 37.4 (SN 37.4, PTS SN iv 240).
1. The First Section on the Series:

The Discourse on Three Qualities “Bhikkhus, possessed of three qualities, women for the most part, with the breakup of the body, after death, are reborn in a state of deprivation, a bad destination, a lower realm, hell. What are the three? [They are: being unvirtuous, being of little learning, and being given over to jealousy.”
Which three?
Here, monks, in the morning time, a woman dwells at home with a mind obsessed by the stain of stinginess.
At the time of midday, she dwells at home with a mind obsessed by envy.
In the evening, with a mind obsessed by sensual lust, she dwells at home.
Possessing these three qualities, monks, a woman for the most part, with the breakup of the body, after death, is reborn in a state of deprivation, a bad destination, a lower realm, even in hell.
This was the fourth.

Saṃyutta Nikāya 37.5 (SN 37.5, PTS SN iv 240) 1. First Subchapter on the Series The Discourse on the Angry One “Bhikkhus, one who is angry is not fit for the attainment of the fruit of stream-entry; one who is not angry is fit for the attainment of the fruit of stream-entry. One who is angry is not fit for the attainment of the fruit of once-returning... of non-returning... of arahantship; one who is not angry is fit for the attainment of the fruit of arahantship. Therefore, bhikkhus, you should train yourselves thus: ‘We will abandon anger whenever it arises. Thus should you train yourselves.”
Then the Venerable Anuruddha approached the Blessed One; having approached, he sat down to one side. Sitting to one side, the Venerable Anuruddha said this to the Blessed One:

"Here, Bhante, with the divine eye, purified and surpassing that of humans, I see a woman who, with the breakup of the body, after death, has reappeared in a state of deprivation, a bad destination, a lower realm, even in hell."
“Bhante, with how many qualities endowed is a woman reborn, after the breakup of the body, after death, in a state of deprivation, a bad destination, a lower realm, or hell?
“Anuruddha, with five qualities endowed is a woman reborn, after the breakup of the body, after death, in a state of deprivation, a bad destination, a lower realm, or hell.
With which five? [The Buddha then enumerates them.]”
“Anuruddha, when a woman possesses these five qualities— she is faithless, shameless, reckless, prone to anger, and lacking in wisdom—
then with the breakup of the body, after death, she is reborn in a state of deprivation, a bad destination, a lower realm, even in hell. This is the fifth.

Saṁyutta Nikāya 37.6 (SN 37.6, PTS SN iv 241) 1. First Subsection on the Summary: The Discourse on Resentment “Bhikkhus, there are these five things that lead to the non-decline of a bhikkhu who is a trainee. What five? He is endowed with faith; he is virtuous; he is learned; he is energetic; and he is wise. These, bhikkhus, are the five things that lead to the non-decline of a bhikkhu who is a trainee.”
“Anuruddha, possessed of five qualities, a woman, with the breakup of the body, after death, is reborn in a state of deprivation, a bad destination, a lower realm, even in hell.
Which five?
She is faithless, she is shameless, she is reckless, she is resentful, and she is of poor wisdom.”
“Anuruddha, a woman endowed with these five qualities, with the breakup of the body, after death, is reborn in a state of deprivation, a bad destination, a lower realm, even in hell.
The sixth.
*Saṃyutta Nikāya* 37.7 (SN 37.7, PTS SN iv 241)
1. The First Section on the Series:

The Discourse on Envy “Anuruddha, possessed of five qualities, a woman, with the breakup of the body, after death, reappears in a state of deprivation, a bad destination, a lower realm, even in hell. Which five? She is envious, she is malicious, she is jealous, she is deceitful, and she is crafty.”
“By which five?
He is faithless, he is shameless, he is reckless, he is envious, and he is unwise.
It is by possessing these five qualities, Anuruddha, that a woman, with the breakup of the body, after death, is reborn in a state of deprivation, a bad destination, a lower realm, even in hell.”
Seventh.
Saṃyutta Nikāya 37.8 (SN 37.8, PTS SN iv 241) 1.
First Subsection on Repetition (Paṭhama-peyyāla-vagga)
The Discourse on the Miserly:
“Anuruddha, possessed of five qualities, a woman, with the breakup of the body, after death, reappears in a state of deprivation, a bad destination, a lower realm, even in hell.
Which five? [Text follows].”
“He is faithless, he is shameless, he is reckless, he is stingy, and he is unwise.
Anuruddha, a woman endowed with these five qualities...
[is reborn] in a state of deprivation, a bad destination, a lower realm, even in hell.”

The Discourse on Transgressions:

“Anuruddha, when a woman possesses five qualities... she is reborn in a state of deprivation, a bad destination, a lower realm, or hell. What are these five? [The text continues with the list of transgressions.]”
“He is faithless, he is shameless, he is reckless, he is unfaithful, and he is lacking in wisdom.
Anuruddha, it is by possessing these five qualities that a woman... [as before] ...is reborn.
The ninth.

Saṁyutta Nikāya 37.10 1. First Subsection on the Summary The Discourse on the Immoral One “Bhikkhus, there are these four kinds of persons found existing in the world. What four? The immoral person who does not understand as they really are the danger in immorality and the benefit in the development of the mind; the immoral person who understands as they really are the danger in immorality and the benefit in the development of the mind; the moral person who does not understand as they really are the danger in morality and the benefit in the development of the mind; and the moral person who understands as they really are the danger in morality and the benefit in the development of the mind. These, bhikkhus, are the four kinds of persons found existing in the world.”
“Anuruddha, when a woman possesses five qualities, she is reborn in hell...
Which five?
She is faithless, shameless, reckless, immoral, and unwise.”
“Anuruddha, a woman who is possessed of these five qualities... [is reborn] in hell.
Tenth. Saṃyutta Nikāya 37.11 (SN 37.11, PTS SN iv 242)

The Discourse on Laziness:
“Anuruddha, when a woman possesses five qualities... she is reborn in hell.
Which five? [The text continues as follows:]”
“Anuruddha, when a woman possesses these five qualities— she is faithless, shameless, reckless, lazy, and lacking in wisdom—
she is reborn in a state of deprivation, a bad destination, a lower realm, even in hell. (The twelfth.)

Saṃyutta Nikāya 37.13 (SN 37.13, PTS SN iv 242) 1. First Subsection on Repetition The Discourse on Lack of Mindfulness "Bhikkhus, when lack of mindfulness is present within, the mind does not become concentrated; one does not understand as it really is: ‘This is suffering. One does not understand as it really is: ‘This is the origin of suffering. One does not understand as it really is: ‘This is the cessation of suffering. One does not understand as it really is: ‘This is the way leading to the cessation of suffering. When lack of clear comprehension is present within, the mind does not become concentrated; one does not understand as it really is: ‘This is suffering.
